值得閱讀的理由

  • 深刻剖析台灣1980至1990年代泡沫經濟狂潮下，兩大傳奇「暴發戶」唐日榮與黃任中的崛起歷程與極致奢華的人生百態。
  • 生動還原荒誕卻真實的金錢遊戲：從自稱軍火商的「選美皇帝」純金排場，到科技先鋒轉身成為操盤數十億的「股市大戶金主」。
  • 借古鑑今，透過兩位風雲人物晚年資產散盡、官司纏身的悲劇結局，揭示財富、權力與欲望交織下的深刻警示。

摘要

時代狂潮下的兩大「暴發戶」縮影

作者指出，「暴發戶」在學術定義上指在極短時間內累積巨額財富並以俗氣方式炫富的人。1980至1990年代的台灣迎來泡沫經濟，熱錢湧入、新台幣大幅升值，社會瀰漫著揮金如土的狂熱氣氛。在那個金錢淹腳目的時代，唐日榮與黃任中成為最具話題性的暴發戶象徵。兩人背景與炫富手法截然不同，卻同樣熱愛美女環繞，且晚年皆落入極其悲涼的境地：唐日榮晚年窮困潦倒，身故時資產僅剩七千元新台幣；黃任中則淪為巨額欠稅大戶，遭法院查封拍賣的名貴古董字畫更全被證實為贗品。

從赤貧補教老師到揮金如土的「選美皇帝」唐日榮

唐日榮生於1940年，隨父親遷台後曾是一名貧困的補習班英文老師，過著連牛肉麵都吃不起的生活。1970年代他跨足中東貿易，自稱在留英期間結識薩達姆，並於兩伊戰爭期間擔任「中東軍火商」累積暴利；儘管外界推測其第一桶金實源於紡織配額，但在浮躁社會中無人深究真假。1985年起，唐日榮展開鋪張的炫富大秀：打造純金名片、價值450萬的純金麻將、購入連轉彎都困難的超長型勞斯萊斯並聘請數十名保鑣。1987年他創辦中華民國選美協會並自封「選美皇帝」，身穿特製大元帥禮服，在自家龍椅上檢閱比基尼佳麗；即便因踩踏珍稀動物標本遭國際抨擊，他仍狂妄地將動物皮毛全換成純金雕塑反擊。

權貴之後轉型科技先鋒與「股市金主」黃任中

另一位主角黃任中同樣出生於1940年，為國民黨元老黃少谷的獨子。年少叛逆、曾被列入不良少年名冊的他，赴美接受嚴格軍校教育後返台創業。抱持著「政治太髒、金錢最乾淨」的想法，他從小規模電視維修廠做起，逐步發展為大型電子裝配廠，並成功引進美商RCA在台設立電路板工廠，奠定台灣電子產業擺脫日本技術壟斷的基礎。1984年底，黃任中以每股17.5元買進遠東航空股票，耐心等待十年後以每股225元售出，狂賺56億新台幣，躍居全球華人富豪榜。坐擁龐大資本的他隨即轉身成為幕後巨擘，大方資助雷伯龍、榮安邱等股市四大天王，成為呼風喚雨的「股市大戶製造機」。

================================================

When it comes to the term "nouveau. riche," the academic definition refers. to people who become wealthy in a very. short period of time. In a way, it’s. a term with classist undertones,. implying that you may have started from. a lower social class, but after gaining. unimaginable wealth, you start showing. off in tacky ways. If you use Chinese. slang to describe it, that would be " tuhao." However, I personally believe. that being "tacky" has nothing to do. with social class; for example, look at. our U.S. President. For Taiwanese. people, who are the "nouveau riche" figures that left a deep impression on. you? Today, we are going to introduce. two gentlemen who rose to prominence in. the 1980s, an era of rapid wealth. accumulation in Taiwan. By the 1990s,. their various flamboyant displays made. headlines, making them the talk of that. decade. These two individuals are Tang. Jih-jung and Huang Jen-chung. Their. backgrounds and ways of showing off. were completely different, but they had. one thing in common: they both loved. beautiful women and were always. surrounded by them. Furthermore, in. their later years, they both met the. same tragic fate. One ended up. destitute, passing away with only 7,000. NT dollars in assets and his family. gone. The other became a major tax. delinquent, with nearly all his. property seized; most pitifully, it was. only after the court seized his. valuable antique paintings that they. discovered they were all forgeries. These two famous Taiwanese "nouveau. riche" figures were essentially the. embodiment of the 1990s bubble economy. How exactly did they rise to power, how. do they define the term "nouveau riche,. " and why did they end up in such bleak. circumstances? Hi, this is Xiao Niu. Welcome to "Xiao Niu Talks Finance." To. tell the story of these two "nouveau. riche" figures, we’ll start by. introducing Tang Jih-jung. He was born. in 1940, with his hometown in Chongqing. , China, and came to Taiwan with his. father during the Civil War. After. graduating from university, Tang. Jih-jung's first job was as an English. teacher at a cram school. He once told. the media how poor he was back then; he. rode a beat-up, constantly breaking. motorcycle to teach, didn't have enough. money for beef noodles—only beef. broth noodles—and lived in a tiny,. cramped room that could only fit a bed,. a desk, and a wardrobe. In the 1970s,. relying on the meager savings he had. built up as a cram school teacher, he. started getting into the Middle East. trade business. The following story. sounds a bit like bragging. He claimed. that while studying in the UK, he met. the future Iraqi president, Saddam. Hussein, and during the Iran-Iraq War,. he handled arms deals for Iraq, calling. himself the "King of the Middle East." All of this was just his own account,. and no one ever verified it. Media. reports later suggested that his first. pot of gold didn't come from Middle. Eastern arms at all, but from textile. export quotas. In short, why did Tang. Ri-rong become wealthy overnight? Looking back now, no one really cared. about the truth of the story. Even back. then, no one questioned whether it was. true or false; the fact that he was. incredibly rich was genuine. People. only cared that he looked wealthy, not. how he actually became wealthy. The. protagonist of our other story, Huang. Ren-zhong, was also born in 1940. Compared to Tang Ri-rong, his family. background was much more prominent—he. was the only son of KMT heavyweight. Huang Shao-gu. Who was Huang Shao-gu? He served as Minister of Foreign. Affairs, Vice Premier of the Executive. Yuan, and eventually President of the. Judicial Yuan, acting as a core advisor. to Chiang Kai-shek. With such a. powerful father to lean on, Huang.

Ren-zhong was headstrong and. domineering from a young age. While. attending night classes at Jianguo High. School, he was constantly getting into. fights and was even put on the Taipei. City Police Department's juvenile. delinquency blacklist. After graduation. , he went to university in the US, but. was expelled for fighting, eventually. transferring to a military academy in. Pennsylvania. It was only under the. strict, militarized education that he. finally settled down to complete his. studies. After Taipei lost diplomatic. recognition in 1971, Huang, citing. patriotic reasons, decided to leave the. US and return to Taiwan. Despite being. the son of a high-ranking official, he. never had any intention of entering. politics. He once said, "Politics is. too dirty. Money is the cleanest thing. —I love money." So, he started his. own business. He began by opening a. small repair shop, handling TV repairs. for the American company RCA. Unexpectedly, the business grew,. expanding from TV repairs until his. small shop eventually became a large. electronics assembly plant. He even. successfully persuaded the boss of RCA. to come. They set up a factory in. Taiwan to produce circuit boards,. helping the Taiwanese electronics. industry break free from Japanese. technical monopolies. From this. perspective, Taiwan's current. electronics success owes a key debt to. Huang Ren-zhong. In 1979, the. government lifted foreign exchange. controls, and hot money began to pour. into Taiwan. The New Taiwan Dollar. appreciated from 40 to 24.5 against the. US Dollar, marking the beginning of. Taiwan's era of extreme extravagance. When society had more money than it. could spend, someone needed to embody. that image of wealth, and Tang Jih-jung. seized this opportunity. In 1985, he. began showing off his stretch Cadillac. limousine in front of media cameras. A. year later, claiming to be an arms. dealer, he appeared on the mainstream. TV programs of the time, flaunting gold. jewelry worth tens of millions of NT. dollars. That wasn't all; he brought. gold-crafted furniture, statues, ingots. , and bricks into the studio, leaving. the host and audience stunned. From. then on, Tang Jih-jung became a. household name. Just how rich was he? In 1993, factory-imported Rolls-Royce. luxury cars officially arrived in. Taiwan, each costing over ten million. NT dollars. At the time, fewer than 50. people in Taiwan owned a Rolls-Royce,. and their identities were all kept. confidential. The rumors on the street. listed Rolls-Royce owners like the Koo. family of Chinatrust, the Wang family. of the Rebar Group, and this mysterious. arms dealer, Tang Jih-jung, standing. alongside these tycoons. The craziest. part was that his Rolls-Royce was a. super-stretched version bought from an. Arab noble, extended by three sections. between the wheels; it was so long it. struggled to make turns. Being this. conspicuous meant he needed protection,. so he hired dozens of bodyguards at his. own expense to follow him everywhere. Furthermore, his business cards were. made of gold, and even his mahjong set. was pure gold, reportedly worth 4.5. million NT dollars. In 1987, with too. much money and a love for beauty, Tang. realized pageants were a good business,. so he founded the Republic of China. Pageant Association and revived. contests that had been suspended for 20. years. From 1988 to 1995, Miss China,. Miss Universe, and Miss International. pageants were held annually, all hosted. by Tang himself, always wearing his own. self-designed outfits. Wearing a grand. marshal-style dress uniform, the media. dubbed this attire the "Tang Jih-jung. Suit." Next, Tang Ri-long would hold. press conferences in his own home,. sitting on his personal dragon throne,.

surrounded by lion heads, tiger skins,. and a group of beauty pageant. contestants in bikinis—it was just. like an ancient emperor choosing his. concubines! That is how he earned the. title of "Beauty Emperor." However,. fame invites trouble. In November 1993,. National Geographic published photos of. him stepping on lion and tiger. specimens, triggering U.S. conservation. groups to hold hearings in Congress and. directly criticize Taiwan's. conservation policies. What was. originally just a gaudy display of. wealth ended up escalating into an. international incident, and Tang. Ri-long was immediately bombarded with. criticism from all sides. But to Tang. Ri-long, money could do anything! So,. he replaced the real lion heads under. his feet with golden animal sculptures. His solution wasn't to put them away,. but to replace the entire set with. solid gold ones. By the way, this man. didn't care about being insulted, but. there were two things you couldn't. touch: first, saying he had no money; second, calling him sexually impotent. Whoever dared to criticize him on these. two points—At the same time, on the. other side of the glitzy and glamorous. Taipei, Huang Ren-zhong was doing. business in a completely different way. than Tang Ri-long. At the end of 1984,. he bought 25 million shares of Far. Eastern Air Transport from his. brother-in-law, the founder Hu Tong-jin. , at 17.5 NTD per share, and then. waited for ten whole years. In 1995, he. sold them to AIG and China Development. Corporation at 225 NTD per share,. instantly making 5.6 billion NTD, which. landed him at number 214 on the Forbes. global list of wealthiest ethnic. Chinese. With this fortune, Huang. Ren-zhong immediately became a major. financier. Who exactly did this. big-name financier lend his money to? The answer is those stock market " whales." So-called "whales" was a. specialized term in the 1990s, which we. covered in our episode on the four. kings of the stock market. These whales. held massive amounts of capital and. were almost unstoppable in the stock. market. Lei Bo-long, Zhan Xiao-shou,. Rong An-qiu, and A-Bu-La—these four. kings and others with famous names in. the stock market all had dealings with. Huang Ren-zhong; he was the financier. behind them. Some have described him as. the "kingmaker of the market whales." Why was Huang Ren-zhong so generous to. these market whales, giving them money. whenever they asked? Because as long as. Huang Ren-zhong considered you a friend. , he would go through fire and water. for you. People describe Huang. Ren-chung’s way of making friends as. being like Lu Zhishen: you drink from a. big bowl, and I’ll eat meat by the. mouthful. But Huang Ren-chung didn't. just lend his money to anyone. As a. financier, he had four rules: first, he. wouldn't lend to anyone he didn't know; second, the interest was fixed at 7 NT. dollars per 10,000 per day, with no. discounts; third, don't even bring up. amounts under 100 million, because he. had no time for petty, small-scale. loans; and finally, anyone who borrowed. from him had to give him a cut if their. stocks made a profit. These rules seem. reasonable, but his first rule about. only lending to acquaintances meant. that everyone he lent money to was a. close friend. When the stocks made. money, everyone was happy to share the. profits, and Huang Ren-chung would take. a significant cut. But when people lost. money due to bad trades, as long as it. wasn't malicious, he felt it was. difficult to cut them off because of. their friendship. Whenever he didn't. cut them off, those losses became his. own. Huang Ren-chung admitted he lost. quite a bit, but because they were. friends asking for help, he really. couldn't refuse, so he had to keep.

playing the role of financier. For. example, Weng Da-ming, who was a. formidable figure in the stock market. back then, often borrowed money from. Huang Ren-chung to speculate on stocks,. with amounts ranging from 500 million. to 800 million. The result of doing. this was that every stock market crash. and storm ended up hitting Huang. Ren-chung directly. In 1988, Finance. Minister Kuo Wan-jung announced the. capital gains tax; the Taiwan stock. market collapsed with no liquidity,. almost all major players were wiped out. , and Huang Ren-chung suffered heavy. losses as well. Later, when several. stock manipulation cases broke out, the. major players owed him billions more. By 1997, he hit the Asian Financial. Crisis, and the over 10 billion he had. lent to corporate groups like Hualon,. Feng-an, and Kuo Zui Motors were all. locked up. Besides lending money to. others for speculation, Huang Ren-chung. certainly played the market himself,. and his mindset was consistent with. those major players: short-term. speculation. He believed that if he. could get a 3%spread on a stock. purchase, he would cash out without. hesitation and never look back. Huang. Ren-chung rarely studied a company's. fundamentals when trading; his. reasoning was that decent, well-run. companies don't necessarily see their. stock prices rise, whereas the prices. of lousy companies often skyrocket. From the perspective of modern. investment and financial management,. this is a truly bizarre philosophy. However, from another angle, for. someone with as much cash on hand as. him, the stock market wasn't an. investment tool—it was a money game. Tang Jih-jung mentioned earlier, what. everyone remembers most about them is. the women. Unlike some. second-generation officials who put on. a grand front but live a scandalous. private life, Huang Jen-chung never hid. his lust and womanizing nature from. start to finish. He was married four. times in total, but outside of these. four marriages, the number of his. flings was countless. He once publicly. stated, "I have four great passions in. life: beautiful women, fine wine,. sports cars, and luxury mansions; I. couldn't live without any of them." Although he outwardly felt that each. was indispensable, looking at his. priorities, beautiful women were always. ranked first. When reporters once. visited Huang Jen-chung's mansion,. everyone there was female, except for. the reporter and Huang himself. These. women surrounding him were all required. to respectfully call him "Master." He. categorized the women around him into. six levels: the highest level was. family, followed in order by. girlfriends, goddaughters, female. confidantes, female disciples, and. employees. He had long ago written his. will, clearly stating in black and. white who would inherit his wine and. who would inherit his paintings. The. women named in the will were all. thrilled to be on the list. As for why. he divided them into these six levels,. and what the meaning behind these. levels was, Huang Jen-chung never. explained it—he left that for you to. guess. Among all the women who. surrounded him, the most tragic one is. Pauline Chan. She was a Hong Kong.

starlet and one of Huang Jen-chung's. most doted-upon goddaughters; their. ambiguous relationship was often a. topic of media gossip. When she became. addicted to drugs, Huang paid for her. to study abroad and encouraged her to. quit, but her condition went from bad. to worse, with scandals, accidents, and. recurring mental health issues. In 2002. , one month after giving birth to a. baby boy, she took her own life at just. 29 years old. There are many theories. about why she was driven to such a path. , but most public opinion always. circles back to the tangled. relationship she had with Huang. Jen-chung. Looking back, many people's. first impression of Huang Jen-chung was. that he was extravagant and debauched,. but he actually had his own logic for. spending money. He would only spend big. on things that held their value or even. appreciated, like paintings,. calligraphy, or antiques. He never. hesitated to spend on those, but if you. asked him to buy designer clothes or. expensive meals costing thousands,. he’d politely decline. Huang's most. famous goddaughter, Hsiao Pan, once. said that he liked to scavenge, using. old bottles to hold his expensive. foreign liquor. He wore budget brands,. snapped up sales at supermarkets,. smoked cigarettes down to his. fingertips, and would even take all the. complimentary toiletries when staying. in hotels abroad. It is hard to imagine. that these are the behaviors of a. billionaire who had tens of billions in. cash and private jets at his disposal. In some ways, Huang Jen-chung was also. a stubborn man, one who wouldn't even. spare his own body. A business owner. once mentioned that what left the. deepest impression was his heart. surgery years ago. The doctor. explicitly told him no sex for three. months, but he insisted on showing his. prowess within a month, later telling. others he took Viagra just to lower his. blood sugar. This man spent his whole. life challenging even his own body. We’ve told the story up to this point. ; their lives as tycoons have pretty. much come to an end. Speaking of their. later years, the only way to describe. them is miserable. First, let’s talk. about Tang Jih-jung. Two years later,. the Art Association posted a missing. person notice in the paper, hoping he. would come forward to face his. financial situation. Only then did. everyone realize that Tang not only. owed a mountain of debt, but his health. was also in critical condition. That. same year, the court ruled that he had. to pay off his massive credit card debt. . The tycoon who once handed out gold. business cards could no longer even. afford his monthly payments. By early. 1998, he was hospitalized for surgery. at Taichung Veterans General Hospital,. and yet, not a single family member. could be found to sign his consent. forms. Finally, on the evening of. October 28th, he passed away from. kidney failure at the age of 58. When. the court went to seize his property,. that solid gold toilet had vanished. into thin air, and that extended. Rolls-Royce was later bought by an. antique dealer in Neihu; the car was. repainted back to its original black,. and now it just gathers dust in the. corner of a warehouse, never hitting. the road again. According to financial. media personality Xie Jin-he, Chang. Jih-lung only had 7,000 yuan to his. name when he died; his life was truly a. microcosm of Taiwan's economic bubble. Instant wealth, living in an illusory. economic bubble, only to end up with. his family scattered and his fortune. lost. Next, let’s talk about Huang. Jen-chung. In his later years, Huang. Jen-chung’s biggest label was "major. tax debtor." The National Tax Bureau. determined he used his investment. company to evade taxes, but Huang.

adamantly refused to admit it. He. believed that legal tax avoidance was a. natural right of the people, and that. the Tax Bureau was acting unlawfully; he would rather go to jail than pay a. single cent of illegal taxes. "I came. from a military academy and can endure. hardship; they think they can scare me. with jail time." When the public. accused him of hiding assets, he. readily admitted that there was indeed. only about 10,000 yuan left in his bank. account, justifying it by saying, "I am. a financier; all my cash has been lent. out, so of course there is no money in. the account." Later, the court seized. his antiques and calligraphy to cover. his tax debts, only to find they were. all fake replicas; this time, he had no. choice but to be detained, and just as. he had claimed, he really went to jail. However, right after his three-month. detention ended, Huang’s health went. from bad to worse. During the 2004. Lunar New Year, despite his illness, he. held one last party at home, but the. money was all gone, and the days of. being surrounded by admirers were long. gone; among the women who stayed, only. his goddaughter, Xiao Pan, was truly by. his side. It was later revealed that. during his heyday, the cash he had lent. out alone reached as high as 10 billion. yuan, but before he passed away, part. of his living expenses came from. friends paying back the debts they owed. him, a few hundred thousand at a time. Although this amount is still. significant to us, it was a massive. drop compared to Huang Jen-chung’s. peak years. In February 2004, Huang. Jen-chung passed away from illness at. the age of 64.   • 生動還原荒誕卻真實的金錢遊戲：從自稱軍火商的「選美皇帝」純金排場，到科技先鋒轉身成為操盤數十億的「股市大戶金主」。
  • 借古鑑今，透過兩位風雲人物晚年資產散盡、官司纏身的悲劇結局，揭示財富、權力與欲望交織下的深刻警示。

摘要

時代狂潮下的兩大「暴發戶」縮影

作者指出，「暴發戶」在學術定義上指在極短時間內累積巨額財富並以俗氣方式炫富的人。1980至1990年代的台灣迎來泡沫經濟，熱錢湧入、新台幣大幅升值，社會瀰漫著揮金如土的狂熱氣氛。在那個金錢淹腳目的時代，唐日榮與黃任中成為最具話題性的暴發戶象徵。兩人背景與炫富手法截然不同，卻同樣熱愛美女環繞，且晚年皆落入極其悲涼的境地：唐日榮晚年窮困潦倒，身故時資產僅剩七千元新台幣；黃任中則淪為巨額欠稅大戶，遭法院查封拍賣的名貴古董字畫更全被證實為贗品。

從赤貧補教老師到揮金如土的「選美皇帝」唐日榮

唐日榮生於1940年，隨父親遷台後曾是一名貧困的補習班英文老師，過著連牛肉麵都吃不起的生活。1970年代他跨足中東貿易，自稱在留英期間結識薩達姆，並於兩伊戰爭期間擔任「中東軍火商」累積暴利；儘管外界推測其第一桶金實源於紡織配額，但在浮躁社會中無人深究真假。1985年起，唐日榮展開鋪張的炫富大秀：打造純金名片、價值450萬的純金麻將、購入連轉彎都困難的超長型勞斯萊斯並聘請數十名保鑣。1987年他創辦中華民國選美協會並自封「選美皇帝」，身穿特製大元帥禮服，在自家龍椅上檢閱比基尼佳麗；即便因踩踏珍稀動物標本遭國際抨擊，他仍狂妄地將動物皮毛全換成純金雕塑反擊。

權貴之後轉型科技先鋒與「股市金主」黃任中

另一位主角黃任中同樣出生於1940年，為國民黨元老黃少谷的獨子。年少叛逆、曾被列入不良少年名冊的他，赴美接受嚴格軍校教育後返台創業。抱持著「政治太髒、金錢最乾淨」的想法，他從小規模電視維修廠做起，逐步發展為大型電子裝配廠，並成功引進美商RCA在台設立電路板工廠，奠定台灣電子產業擺脫日本技術壟斷的基礎。1984年底，黃任中以每股17.5元買進遠東航空股票，耐心等待十年後以每股225元售出，狂賺56億新台幣，躍居全球華人富豪榜。坐擁龐大資本的他隨即轉身成為幕後巨擘，大方資助雷伯龍、榮安邱等股市四大天王，成為呼風喚雨的「股市大戶製造機」。
